_about: Glitch routes for Pokémon that can't be obtained by normal play or trading. Keyed by game, then national dex number. Methods are for English cartridges unless noted.

mewGlitch.name: Mew glitch (trainer escape / Trainer-Fly)
mewGlitch.steps: Stand where a long-range trainer (e.g. the Gambler near Lavender Town, or a Route 24 trainer) will spot you, and open the Start menu and use Fly (or Teleport) on the same step they see you. Fly to Cerulean City and battle the Youngster on Route 25 near Bill's house, making sure he walks up to you. Fly back to Lavender Town and walk west onto Route 8: the Start menu pops up by itself; close it and a level 7 Mew appears.
mewGlitch.warning: Harmless to your save, but follow the steps exactly. Save before starting.

celebiEgg.name: Celebi Egg glitch
celebiEgg.steps: Make a 'bad clone' with the PC box trick (deposit more Pokémon than you've ever deposited in a box), get a Day Care Egg from a Sneasel whose third move is Beat Up, then shuffle the Egg with 'PkMn w/o mail' moves and PC deposits so its move bytes overwrite its species. Hatch it to get Celebi.
celebiEgg.warning: Long and fiddly. It relies on save-corrupting tricks: back up your save first (use an emulator save state or a cartridge backup).

aceSetup.name: Arbitrary code execution (ACE) setup
aceSetup.steps: Get a glitch Egg of species 0x611 (Emerald/RS) or 0x351 (FireRed/LeafGreen) and use it to run code typed into your PC box names. Follow E-Sh4rk's ACE3 tutorial, then use the box-name codes from Sleipnir's lists.
aceSetup.warning: Works on real GBA hardware or the mGBA emulator (other emulators may not be accurate enough). Not for the Switch versions. Keep box 12–14 and the last row of box 11 empty when running codes, keep spare copies of the glitch Egg, and check each code worked before saving.
